title: Automated Lead Engine
audience: Independent developers and solo agencies with a proven campaign who want connected, unattended lead processing without building a custom application.
shortDescription: Connect a proven prospecting process in n8n with current evidence, qualification, enrichment, outreach state, retries, and exception handling.
coreOutcome: Move repetitive lead processing into a workflow while keeping the evidence, state, and stop rules that make the campaign trustworthy.
problem: The campaign is proven, but moving every lead through evidence collection, enrichment, outreach state, and follow-up by hand now consumes too much time.
hook: You have already proved the prospecting decisions. Now the handoffs are wasting your time.
reframe: Workflow automation earns its place after the campaign rules are stable. At that point, manually moving each qualified lead from discovery to evidence collection, enrichment, outreach, follow-up, and state updates becomes the bottleneck. n8n can remove that repetition, but a straight-line workflow is not enough. Real campaigns encounter duplicates, unusable evidence, provider failures, rate limits, replies, bounces, opt-outs, retries, and leads that should stop rather than continue. Automated Lead Engine models those cases explicitly. The workflow carries forward the same evidence-first qualification rules from the lower tiers, adds durable state transitions and exception paths, and treats dry runs, deduplication, suppression, retries, and cost controls as part of the design. This tier is for connecting a method that already works so your attention shifts from moving records between tools to reviewing exceptions and improving the campaign.

delivery.length: Implementation guide for an n8n-based prospecting pipeline from discovery through outreach state and exception handling.
delivery.worksheets: Workflow map, state transitions, provider boundaries, retry and dedupe rules, dry-run checks, cost controls, suppression, and exception review.
delivery.time: Implement after campaign rules are proven, then test in dry-run and supervised modes before unattended processing.

proof.title: A reliable workflow has a defined failure path.
proof.body: Duplicate detection, unusable evidence, provider errors, replies, bounces, opt-outs, and cost limits all have explicit outcomes instead of falling through the happy path.
proof.before: One long automation moves every discovered business toward an email unless something crashes.
proof.after: Each stage can continue, reject, retry, suppress, pause for review, or stop based on recorded state and evidence.

situation: Your qualification method works and the volume now justifies connected workflow automation.
commonFailure: A linear happy-path workflow breaks when duplicates, stale evidence, replies, bounces, provider errors, retries, or cost limits are not modeled.
methodology: Connect discovery, normalization, evidence, qualification, enrichment, outreach, sequence state, suppression, retries, and exception handling in n8n.
capabilities: Build unattended n8n workflows around a proven campaign
Preserve current website evidence and explicit lead state
Control retries, duplicates, costs, replies, bounces, and suppression
contents: Readiness criteria for automating a campaign that already works
Discovery, normalization, current website evidence, and structured qualification
Deduplication, retries, provider failures, and exception paths
Reply, bounce, opt-out, suppression, and stop handling
Dry runs, monitoring, cost controls, and the boundary for a custom application
whoItsFor: Operators with a proven campaign and intermediate automation skills
Developers whose main prospecting burden is repeated tool-to-tool handoffs
Builders ready to operate n8n, APIs, retries, and exception handling
whoItsNotFor: Beginners who have not validated their qualification and outreach rules
Anyone looking for a high-volume blast workflow
Teams that already need database-backed state and controlled concurrency

faqs.question: Why not start here?
faqs.answer: Because automation repeats the decisions you give it. If qualification and evidence rules are weak, this tier only scales the weakness.

faqs.question: Is Google Sheets still the primary state store?
faqs.answer: Yes. At this tier, Sheets remains the visible primary state while n8n owns workflow execution and connected handoffs.

faqs.question: Does it support unattended processing?
faqs.answer: Yes, after testing and only inside defined campaign limits, suppression rules, stop conditions, and monitoring.

faqs.question: When should I move to Tier 4?
faqs.answer: Move up when multiple campaigns, concurrency, auditability, durable recovery, and testing have outgrown a workflow-centered architecture.

stateModel: Google Sheets is primary state; the workflow is the unit of execution
supervision: Unattended processing with monitoring and exception review
technicalBoundary: n8n is the primary orchestrator. Workflow logic owns retries and deduplication. This is not a database-backed custom application.
